name: Question 3
problem: Consider a matrix equation $AB\,x=d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $4\times 4$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $4\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
worked_solution:
Since $A$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${A}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $AB\,x=d$ by ${A}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB\,x & =d \\ {A}^{-1}AB\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{4}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${B}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,x={A}^{-1}\,d$ by ${B}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{4}\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Consider a matrix equation ABx=d, where A and B are 4×4 non-singular matrices, while x and d are 4×1 column vectors. Solve the equation for x.

a
x=A−1dB
b
x=B−1dA−1
c
x=A−1B−1d
d
x=BAd
e
x=B−1A−1d
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since A is not singular, it must have an inverse A−1. Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation ABx=d by A−1, we obtain

ABx=dA−1ABx=A−1dI4Bx=A−1dBx=A−1d.

Since B is not singular, it must have an inverse B−1. Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation Bx=A−1d by B−1, we obtain

Bx=A−1dB−1Bx=B−1A−1dI4x=B−1A−1dx=B−1A−1d.
